sections.name: body
sections.value:
**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES**, round 2 (final under C34), at `b1461b876ddf13894d2635d85af46b958c5ea63e`.

**Fixes:** F001 applies the same state-notice refresh to claimed/full and pending reads. The six-FYI HTTP regression positively verifies a resolved notice omitted from the digest appears marked in its full read. These remain read-only: the new helper reads registry/cached sizes and changes returned copies, not stored FYIs. F002 leaves ordinary queued payloads unnoted and adds the PA line on claim/worker hand-over; the regression checks both FYIs arriving after queueing and a pile consumed before hand-over. The documented direct-typed deferral retains its staged text intentionally for leftover recognition.

**Cap:** N001 now budgets **1,746 bytes for the stall body + two separating bytes + at most 300 for the PA line = 2,048**. It reserves footer/omission space and may omit even the first FYI listing when it will not fit. The updated CI case combines long valid seat IDs, 60 FYIs and seven waiting seats; the store-backed stall test also checks the handed-over body. This bounds displayed text, not preparation.

**Cost delta:** no new timer, poll or process launch site. The existing 60-second presence check, global pending-row scan, claim/re-arm/wake costs and full-registry FYI-carrier snapshots retain the [round-1 budget](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/pull/214#issuecomment-6757680890).

Full/pending reads now add the O(S) registry snapshot/map and batch-copy work **only if** their batch contains a relevant local daemon state notice; otherwise just the batch predicate. Each snapshot still includes the schema PRAGMA, all registry rows and size-board lookups.

The PA-line computation is not strictly once per delivered turn: `arrive()` still prepares `direct` before selecting the route, so a queued admission can compute and discard a line, then compute again on claim. Each actual claim/uncached worker attempt adds a role PK read and schema guard; a PA can additionally take the global backlog aggregation, full registry read, matching/sorting and synchronous repository file walks. The worker calls this before pane/probe/backoff decisions. Unchanged bodies are not cached, so those reads can recur at the existing retry cadence; no new work is added to empty claims.

The worker's new 64-job map preserves changed text while resident, avoiding re-querying/reformatting those retries. It retains **whole bodies, not merely the 300-byte line**, has no byte budget and still clones a remembered body on reuse. Admission also clones the message to prepare `direct`. Restart/eviction boundaries are not a persistent retry-text guarantee.

**P214-N001 remains a named C34 follow-up**, now in Known limits: global scans, full-registry reads, filesystem work and retained/copied payloads have no measured large-store ceiling. The cap and small behavior tests do not establish that ceiling or justify “cheap at today's fleet size.” No demonstrated normal-use cost breach or remaining performance blocker found; no redesign or extra fixtures requested.

**Exact-head proof:** [CI 42747508415](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42747508415), Rust job `129603028970`, upload artifact **13731519016**, head metadata verified: **2,378 executed passed**, zero failures/errors; six skips separately reported by nextest. JUnit names the queued-hand-over, digest full-read, delivered-cap and existing stall/F170 regressions, plus all six spawn guards. Node22 npm **2,281 passed, six skipped**; Node24, Rust lint and final delivers succeed. Worktree clean, matching GitHub head/CLEAN. No local build/test/probe, mutation or synthetic traffic. **After-deploy reading remains owed; no new before/after measurement is claimed.**
